assessment.rationale: Under the institutional/regional lens, the supplied records provide general institutional context but not enough deployment-specific context to establish regional feasibility. CISA CPG and NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 records describe recommended brute-force-relevant controls such as MFA, alerting after unsuccessful logins, system-enforced login prevention, unique credentials, and account lockout or delay (E_23_312B9513BCEE9B9D, E_23_B21FAA9377991F05, E_23_EBCAB9508641E703, E_25_FE58E4FCF044EDE3). MITRE ATT&CK M1029 describes remote storage, centralized log management, IDS/IPS log forwarding, immutable storage, and encryption/access-control practices (E_12_D8076704AE363FE2). These support general governance and auditability context. Crossref records show IDS/IPS publication activity, including a positive publication trend from 2021 to 2024, but the trend record explicitly states that this does not establish deployment maturity, operational effectiveness, or causal mitigation effectiveness (E_33_A707006877BFD1C2, E_29_8E495DC2A98305B1, E_29_BAD6581A8E96027C, E_29_CA00E63DF08A6FC1). The frozen deployment context has no region, organization type, budget context, or infrastructure context, so regulatory compatibility, data sovereignty, compliance burden, cross-border constraints, and deployment-specific implementation barriers cannot be assessed. Therefore, institutional/regional feasibility is neither supported nor materially challenged; it is indeterminate due to missing deployment context.
